transcript:
Header:
Date/Time: 2025-07-14 09:30 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Location: Zoom
Recording id: ff-20250714-87b2
Attendees: Alex Moran (Redwood AE), Sanjay Iyer (Redwood SE), Lina Park (Redwood CSM), Priya Menon (CTO, NimbusHealth), Marco Ruiz (Platform Eng), Jenna Lowe (ML Eng)
Artifacts referenced: shared deck (https://redwood.example/decks/nimbus-dedicated-poc.pdf), burst test plan (link shared in chat), traffic-replay instructions doc.

Summary:
- Quick review of last week's pilot metrics (latency p50/p95/p99, token throughput).
- Discussed autoscaling policy for Dedicated pool: min nodes, max nodes, scale-up step, burst/headroom.
- Agreed on 8-hour controlled burst test and data export for replay.
- Action items assigned around traffic export, configuration, and cost estimates.

Topics:
- Metric anomalies on Monday spike
- Prefix/KV cache hit rates and implications for scaling
- Priority queueing (critical production vs low-pri batch)
- Fallback model variants for cost control

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex (AE): ok good morning everyone thanks for joining, quick roll call...
[00:18] Priya (CTO): hey all, sorry joining a bit from a weird connection, hope you can hear me, yes good morning.
[00:35] Sanjay (SE): can hear you Priya, all good. we'll go through the numbers first then the autoscale.
[00:45] Jenna (ML Eng): just flagging i'm on mobile, audio might cut.
[01:05] Alex: perfect, so slide 3 in the deck— last week we saw average token throughput at 12k tokens/min, p95 latency around 420ms for the 4k sequence tests, p99 spiked to 1.2s during Monday peak.
[01:32] Marco: yeah that p99 spike is the concern, we saw timeouts in our integration tests. it looks correlated with concurrent long chat sessions.
[01:50] Sanjay: quick note— the spike lines up with low KV cache hit rates. we saw a drop to 18% hits vs baseline 62% when many unique user contexts showed up.
[02:10] Priya: is that because of new prompt variations from the pilot user set? we did change some prompt routing last week.
[02:25] Jenna: we added richer patient summaries and appended context blobs, so more unique prefixes.
[02:40] Alex: ok that explains cache churn. for autoscaling, we need to plan for cache warmup cost — scaling too slowly causes p99 blowouts, scaling too aggressively increases GPU-min cost.
[03:05] Marco: we want a policy that handles predictable daily peaks and unpredictable bursts — also need hard caps because of our budget constraints.
[03:22] Sanjay: proposed config: min 2 GPUs, target steady 6 GPUs, max 20 GPUs, with a burst allowance to 30 for short windows. scale-up policy step: +2 nodes per minute, scale-down after 10 minutes of low CPU/req.
[03:51] Priya: that max 30 seems high, can you justify?
[04:00] Sanjay: rationale: burst headroom prevents tail latency from blowing up when cache gets cold; we modeled token distribution and 30 GPUs keeps p99 under 900ms in most sims. but the 30 is a short-burst cap (configured as burst_capacity) not sustained.
[04:28] Marco: cost-wise that's concerning, we need to estimate GPU-min and dollar impact.
[04:36] Alex: we ran a quick cost sim in the deck — rough numbers: baseline ~480 GPU-min/day at 6 GPUs, an 8-hour burst with average additional 12 GPUs adds ~5,760 GPU-min. we'll provide precise billing projections.
[04:58] Jenna: can we set priority queues so non-critical batch inference uses lower-cost nodes or preemptible?
[05:15] Sanjay: yes, Redwood Dedicated supports routing by priority tag. low-priority can be routed to preemptible-backed pool with lower SLOs, or to quantized model variants to save GPU memory.
[05:36] Priya: what's the fallback flow if Dedicated capacity is exhausted? auto-failover to hosted?
[05:45] Alex: correct, policy option to fallback to hosted-compatible model (for example smaller opt-quant variant) in another region — the platform will fail open or queue based on config.
[06:02] Marco: we want clear SLAs for that — who owns costs when fallback happens?
[06:10] Alex: that's typically part of deal terms — for the pilot, Redwood will log fallback events and we can set a trial rule where Redwood covers incremental hosted cost for testing, but we need to scope it in the pilot addendum.
[06:30] Priya: ok makes sense.
[06:38] Jenna: about the cache warmup — can we pre-warm KV with the traffic replay?
[06:45] Sanjay: absolutely, traffic replay with prefix frequency will warm caches. we recommend a phased replay: night-one 10% traffic, night-two 50%, then full-day rehearse before the burst.
[07:05] Marco: we'll provide the logs but need a template for what you need.
[07:10] Alex: we'll share the replay instructions doc after the call.
[07:22] (15:00) [Note: speaker label glitch — "Speaker 2" shows up next]
[07:36] Speaker 2: uh yeah just to add— the team should consider quantized variants for the heavy batch jobs, 8-bit quantization drops memory and improves throughput.
[07:52] Priya: we had a question about model variants — will latency for quantized be noticeably worse?
[07:58] Sanjay: usually slight diff: 5–12% higher per-token latency but higher throughput; depends on layer fusion and kernel selection. we'll benchmark for Nimbus models during the burst test.
[08:25] Alex: next, autoscale cooldown and growth rate — if we scale too fast we fragment cache, too slow and latency spikes. proposed cooldown 10m, aggressive growth window if sustained >70% GPU util for 2 minutes.
[08:50] Marco: what about sudden small spikes that last 30–90s? scale-up latency itself is 30–90s, so we may need a buffer via burst_capacity.
[09:05] Sanjay: correct — burst_capacity is immediate allocation from reserved buffer; it's fast but we limit total burst minutes to control cost. that was the 48 GPU-min cap idea discussed in the chat.
[09:20] Priya: can we run a safe experiment: 8-hour burst window during our low-risk hours where we intentionally mimic peak traffic? we can monitor errors and latencies.
[09:32] Alex: yes, Redwood proposes Wed 2025-07-16 02:00–10:00 UTC for the controlled burst test.
[09:40] Jenna: confirm timezone please, that overlaps our dev ops window, ok.
[09:48] Marco: we'll need clear abort criteria — e.g., if p99 > 2s for 5 consecutive minutes or error rate >1% then abort.
[10:00] Sanjay: yep we'll codify abort triggers and a rollback plan that transitions traffic to fallback variant.
[10:12] Priya: also want detailed logs— request ids, KV miss rate, queue length — we need to ingest them to our datalake for postmortem.
[10:22] Alex: agreed — we'll enable richer tracing and share the S3 link to the log bundle.
[10:30] Marco: on the security side, for Dedicated we need KMS proofs and SOC2 artifacts — can we get a short security checklist?
[10:40] Lina (CSM): yes I'll follow up with the security pack. we have a stubbed checklist for VPC/private deployments.
[10:50] Priya: will our compliance team require on-prem agent? we don't want to fully push on-prem yet, but need to know the gap.
[11:00] Alex: for pilot we can run in Redwood Private VPC with customer-managed keys; an on-prem agent is optional and takes more lead time. We'll map the gap list.
[11:15] Marco: coming back to autoscale parameters — can you share the sensitivity matrix you mentioned? how token length distribution affects GPU needs?
[11:25] Sanjay: yes, slide 7 has approximate multipliers: avg 2k tokens/session uses ~1.2X base memory vs 512 tokens; 4k seqs require more KV and reduce batchable concurrency, so per-request GPU time increases. We'll attach a CSV of sims.
[11:45] Jenna: can we also try adaptive batching with shorter latency windows? we saw some improvements in internal tests.
[11:55] Sanjay: Redwood runtime supports adaptive batching and cutoff heuristics; we can enable an adaptive policy that trades a bit of p50 for improved qps. We'll include that in the test matrix.
[12:12] Alex: ok quick check on timeline and who owns what — Marco will export the 3-day traffic sample and share by Thursday, July 16. Redwood (Sanjay/Alex) will configure the burst policy and run the 8-hour test Wed July 16/17 (TBD) and produce a results bundle by Friday. CSM Lina to share security checklist and replay instructions.
[12:38] Marco: agreed. also request a short cost projection table under two scenarios: conservative (no burst) and burst-8hr.
[12:45] Alex: will do, we'll include GPU-min and estimated $ range.
[12:52] Priya: thanks — one last note: can we enable a canary route for 5% traffic to the fallback model during burst? reduces outage risk.
[13:02] Sanjay: yes, that's in the rollout policy — canary 5% then ramp if stable.
[13:12] (Short crosstalk and some audio dropouts)
[13:38] Priya: sorry going on phone briefly — 
[13:50] Alex: before we close, any blockers?
[14:00] Jenna: just need the replay template and we'll be good.
[14:08] Marco: one more: please call out the exact metrics you'll publish post-test — we expect p50/p95/p99, error rate, KV hit rate, node count timeline and cost.
[14:25] Alex: yes we'll publish a one-page results summary and full logs.
[14:35] Priya: ok thanks team.
[14:40] Alex: thanks everyone — we'll follow up in email with links and action items.
[14:50] (Meeting ends)
